utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please be asked to come closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you get closer to the microphone. The interpreters are having a hard time for you -- hearing you. And first of all, what year was this second time-period and -- the second time-period where I believe you said the 15th of April?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you recall what type of ribbons were used during this time-period?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Yellow, blue, and red.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: During 1999 -- well, first of all, I want to ask you about an individual named Nebojsa Minic. Was he a member of the Pec secretariat in 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: No. I don't know exactly how much time he spent with us. I know -- well, about two months, August and perhaps September; and then he smashed up a kiosk in a street in Pec, and since then I've never seen him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say he wasn't in the police, was he -- was he let go out of the police force?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to focus for a time-period on the KLA. Did you have occasion to hear any public pronouncements by representatives of the KLA prior to 1999; and if so, what precisely did you hear, when did you hear it, and who was with you when you heard it?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: I saw Adem Demaqi in his family, or rather, in the family home of Gashi Zenun. Policeman Jankovic was with me. The three of us were sitting in a room and a statement was on TV Tirana to the effect that Kosovo cannot be freed at all or cleansed at all from the Serbs unless the international community is provoked so that all the Siptars would leave the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, and then by displaying a humanitarian catastrophe the world would react and their objectives would be accomplished. I remember that because Gashi Zenun and Jankovic Radojica were making comments about that. And right now we see what the situation is in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can move on. Did you ever eye-witness any KLA tactics with regards to civilians?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: KLA tactics boiled down to the following. They would provoke an incident, cause an incident, then they would seek shelter in villages where there were civilians, and in this way they would show the people that the police was carrying out repression against them. I had this one particular case while I worked at the Celopek police department. A person by the name of Kelmendi from the village of Kosuric reported that he had been mistreated in his family home by the members of the KLA, that is. We went to the actual site, to his home, and as we took statements from his family they told us that they had set out in the direction of the village of Glodjane. The patrol went to the village of Glodjane, to be more precise they went to the church within the village itself. We parked our vehicle, and at that moment a Mercedes came by, four persons ran out of it and opened fire at us. We could not open fire because behind them there were civilians who were working in the fields. On that occasion a policeman was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What was the KLA's practice with respect to uniforms?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: As I said, about the Lodz village, some 15 of them were wearing the police uniform because at that time it was possible to get hold of police uniforms, just buy them. But for the most part they discarded their own uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what was the KLA practice with respect to their own casualties, as you witnessed?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: In many, many cases they carried their own wounded and dead away, they didn't leave them behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now focusing on your own family, did any of your family members or relatives endure attacks by the KLA in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In 1998 early in July, maybe the 2nd or 3rd of July, we left our family home in our village precisely because of that and we moved to a suburb of Pec. That last incident that happened to my family and myself happened, although prior to that we had good neighbourly relations with the surrounding families, three of our Albanian neighbours came with a tractor to do our fields so that we would not be exposed by working outside. They expected that no one would open fire on them; however, on that day fire was opened on them from the direction of Streoc village. And the next day we moved out. Our family was not the only one to leave, the Paunovic family, Jokic, Vukovic families and the Drmanovics and Vujisics from Zlopek village also left and it turned out to have been a good idea because that same night Lakos Paunovic was kidnapped and to this day no one knows what happened to him. Before that they also kidnapped three of my neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Who were those neighbours and what ethnicity were they?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Zeko Gutic was an employee of EPS.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If the interpreter heard correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was a Muslim. Vucic Vukovic was from Dugocak village very near to mine. And Vuk Vujisic, a child of 15. Nothing is known of their fate either, except that according to some information Vesel Dizdari who was Vukovic's family kum kidnapped them when they were passing by his house and saying hello.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you know of any specific instances where the KLA targeted ethnic Albanians and your home village?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Apart from the information you've already gave us about Mr. Kelmendi, do you know of any other instances where the KLA targeted ethnic Albanians in your home village?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about my village --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The area around [Previous translation continues]... village.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Right. Zenun Gashi a policeman, according to a report made by his wife, was visited at his home by some men. They raped the wife and his daughter aged 12, they took him out to the terrace of the house, beat and abused him, and later took him away. He used to live in Kosuric village. The only reason why they did that was that he had not left the police force. Samija Ademi, another man I used to work with, was involved in an incident at the police station in Celopek when policeman Dragan Bilanovic was killed. He escaped through the woods. He used to work in Celopek police station and lived in Zlopek village some 15 kilometres away. During the night he went to his home, and later I heard that he got away, went abroad, to Switzerland to join his brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you know of any incident involving a Gani Shari?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Gani Shala, is that the man you mean, from Rausic. He had a shop in his own village. Someone fired three or four shells at his house and fired at it with infantry weapons just because the police used to buy things from his shop. And we tried to avoid meeting with our neighbours in our own villages to spare those neighbours later being accused of being spies and to spare them from repressions by KLA members.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did any members of your unit die in the course of 1998 and 1999 in Kosovo-Metohija due to attacks of the KLA; and if so, how many?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Many of them were killed. I don't know the exact number, but 24 perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would that be approximately 24 out of the total 80 that you testified earlier had been part of your unit?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you know how many persons were wounded within your unit during the same time-period in fighting with the KLA?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Many more were wounded, up to 40, around 40, perhaps even more.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could now focus on the time-period in 1998 following the October agreements with the OSCE and onwards, what kind of work did your PJP unit in Pec undertake at that time after the OSCE mission came to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: As the OSCE arrived to Kosovo, I was doing my regular police work in the police station in Celopek, save for the incident in Racak, when an attempt was made to apprehend the group located in that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How did the members of the KLA act after the withdrawal and reduction of the MUP from Kosovo and Metohija pursuant to the agreement with the OSCE?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Would you say that again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How did the members of the KLA act following the withdrawal of MUP pursuant to the October accords and the arrival of the OSCE?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: The KLA started with provocations in towns. They moved from villages to towns.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did their --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: In Pec where I was, there was the incident of the Panda cafe, where six children were killed. Then there was this bomb or hand-grenade thrown onto another cafe called Slavica. No one got killed but people were wounded. So their method was to go in small groups and perpetrate acts of revenge also against Albanians who socialised with Serbs or perhaps even employees of the police as well as against Serbs and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. If we could now move along to the time-period of the NATO bombings. Do you have knowledge of any specific NATO attacks on the territory where you were carrying out your duties and what they hit?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Pec was hit when bombs fell on the barracks of the VJ, which is between a suburb called Brezanik and another one Karagac was targeted, Brezanik, Bijelo Polje, Zagrevanje [phoen], Rugova, Barane, Krusevac, and even one cluster bomb fell close to my house, killing a little girl who was working with her parents making haystacks. She was wounded, injured. I saw her later at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure whether it's killed or injured.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was also Savine Vode, where a bus was moving from Djakovica towards Rozaje in Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: During the time-period of the NATO air war, what were relations like between the police and civilians?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: The relations between the police and civilians was the same as before; it's just that now the police were trying to put civilians under cover when bombing was expected. The police expected that the post office in the centre would be targeted, so as soon as the alert siren was sounded civilians ran for cover -- although, in fact the air-strikes were more or less continuous.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What were the instructions that you received from your superior officers within the MUP regarding treatment of civilians when engaged as part of the PJP?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Before each and every action we were told very clearly to treat civilians with -- in keeping with the highest professional standards, and the same applied to any wounded persons and anyone arrested. They had to be treated professionally and in keeping with all the laws of the Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did members of your unit ever receive any orders from superiors within the MUP to the effect of undertaking to rob or forcibly evict civilians of ethnic Albanian nationality out of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: During the time-period of the NATO war, what did the Pec secretariat of the interior do to try and prevent crimes and uphold public law and order across the territory that it served?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: I used to see police officers in Pec, both in mufti and in uniform, especially in the evenings because there was no street lighting due to air-strikes, and crime incidence was increased. They were working trying to detect and apprehend perpetrators of criminal acts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you ever eye-witness any incidents where a policeman from your unit engaged in any criminal act against a civilian during the course of his duties?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: No. There was this one case that I mentioned before when Minic smashed up a kiosk, but he was removed from the service immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you know any police officer by the name of Zoran Djuricic from Decani?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but Zoran Djuricic only worked in Decani, otherwise he hails from Papic village.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to see him engaged as a member of the PJP at any time during 1999 in the course of any action?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: I think he was not in the PJP at all. I never saw him because they belong to the PJP of Djakovica and I never saw him with that outfit. When I saw him, it was at a check-point when he was working in Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you perhaps know a Vule Mircic of the Decani OUP?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was the chief at the department of internal affairs in Decani. I never saw him in the field either, but I know him because I used to live there and I came frequently -- I went frequently to Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd just like to take a few moments to go through an exhibit and see if we can highlight some points that you might have some personal knowledge or information on. If we could have Exhibit 6D614 up on the screen, and the first item I would like to ask you about is at page 519 of the same, item number -- item number 10. Now, sir, could you first, so that everyone knows what we're talking about here, could you first read the first two sentences of this entry in this overview and tell us if you have any personal knowledge of the same. If you could perhaps zoom in on item number 10, the second from the bottom on the page, that might make it easier.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: "On the 5th of July, 1998, Rados Paunovic from Rausic village left Pec to go to his home and property in Rausic village when he was kidnapped by armed members of the KLA."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: I know this person. We used to be neighbours. I talked about him before and I mentioned his nickname, Lakos Paunovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So is this the incident you told us about earlier when you and your family had to leave the village with several other families and this individual was kidnapped?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if you could just briefly read for us the remainder of that section and highlight for us the perpetrators of the crime against whom charges were filed.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: "An investigation of the crime scene was carried out for safety reasons. "Criminal complaint KU 391/99 was filed against unknown perpetrators as well as an amendment to the complaint. Both of the documents were lodged with the district public prosecutor's office in Pec. This crime of terrorism was committed by Krasniqi Meto, Krasniqi Dino, Dizdari Vesel, Sakaj Resat, Krasniqi Cuf, Krasniqi Iber, Krasniqi Devad, Krasniqi Dzafer, and Krasniqi Avni. All of them lived in Pec municipality." I would like to point out this: With the exception of Dizdari Vesel, they are all from the village of Vranoc to the extent that I can tell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could you find a suitable place to interrupt, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Let me just ask one more question about this point so we can finish up this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you personally know these individuals that you say are from the village of Vranoc?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Meto Krasniqi was the owner of a cafe in Pec, his cousin was killed in 1997 during the attack on the Ozrim police squad. In 1996 I was with the Celopek police squad, on the 28th of August when an attack occurred. That was when these attacks first started, attacks on police squads. At first he was a suspect, but later it became clear that he had been involved in the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Your --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: My apologies. As for Veselj Dizdari, as I mentioned before -- Meto Krasniqi, he was killed after the war because he had committed a number of different crimes in the area, specifically in and around Pec, Decani, and Djakovica. He was the leader of a group known as Crna Ruka, the black arm -- the Black Hand. Veselj Dizdari is a neighbour of mine and he is also the "kum" of Vukovic Vucic. I believe I mentioned him in relation to the kidnapping.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just lastly, this group, Crna Ruka, were they -- what ethnicity were they?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: They were all Albanians, Siptars, at least as far as I know. I had friends over there who were Siptars and based on what they told me I learned that Meto Krasniqi who was passing himself off as a great friend of mine was actually leader of that group.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could have the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Mr. Nikcevic, we will have to break at this stage for half an hour or so; while we have that break, could you please leave the courtroom with the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And we shall resume at five minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nikcevic, just to finish off the area -- the point that we had before the break before moving on. Meto Krasniqi, you said he was killed after the war because he had committed a number of different crimes in the area. Do you know whom he was killed by, if you know? I'm told there was a problem with the translation. I'll try this microphone. To finish up the area that we started before the break, you mentioned that Meto Krasniqi was killed after the war because he had committed a number of different crimes in the area. If you know, could you tell us whom he was killed by, that's if you know.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: I know about what happened in Streoc about this Albanian lady whose name I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think there's still a problem -- I'm asking specifically about the killing of Meto Krasniqi. Do you know whom he was killed by after the war; if you don't, just say so and we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: There's this friend who told me that a man from Streoc had killed him whose daughter Meto had previously raped. I think his last name was Strefaja [phoen] but I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would that have been an ethnic Albanian or another ethnicity surname?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, an Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. If we can move on to page 590 of this exhibit and item number 96 there from Krusevac, Pec, July 1998. I'll wait for it to come up on the screen. One moment. This doesn't appear to be the -- there we go. Now it's up. I believe this part does not have a translation, that might be the confusion. We're getting number 96 from a prior section on the right-hand side of the e-court. For purposes of having everyone able to understand what we're talking about, sir, could you read item number 96 in its entirety and then tell us if you have any -- if you know any of the persons involved in the event that's depicted. A. "Between July and September 1998, several times members of the KLA carried out terrorist attacks on homes, property of Radomila Boskovic from Pec, Krusevac village, Pec municipality. For this reason she had no choice but to move out with her family. After that, members of the KLA took away from the house all movable property and set fire to the house itself. No on-site investigation was carried out because of security concerns. A criminal complaint was filed against unknown perpetrators and served on the public prosecutor's office in Pec."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you know the persons involved and do you have a personal recollection of the incident that is depicted?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: I knew Radomila Boskovic, I worked in the area and the Celopek squad covered Krusevac village as well. The entire Serb population of those villages, such as Krusevac, Dubocak, Rausic, Brolic, Rosulje, and Glodjane left their homes. Some later stayed in Pec and some left for Serbia or Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could move -- it should be 18 pages further in e-court, page 608 of the B/C/S original, item number 183, that's at the bottom of the page, going to the top of the next page. That should be page 608, 183 is the item number or the entry number I guess I should say. It should be page 608, I'm told this is page 683. We should have page 608 and that should only be in the Serbian original. This one is one of the sections that's still being subject of translation. There we go, at the bottom of this page, and since we don't have a translation of this handy, if you could, please, for us, sir, read entry number 183 and when you're done with this page have us -- tell us so we can turn to the next page where it's continued this incident on the 7th of September, 1998, in Dubocak, Pec, item number 183. If we could read that for us, sir, first.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: "Between the 31st of May and the 7th of September 1998 on several occasions, members of the KLA carried out terrorist attacks on Aleksa Stankovic's house, also known as Stankovic Leko, from Dubocak village, Pec municipality, and for this reason he had no choice but to move out with his family." I know this person.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could first off go to the -- well, why don't we do it this way. Do you recall the individual and do you recall the incident? Did you have a personal role in this, could you tell us what that was.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: I talked about incidents when Jovanovic was killed that same month in Celopek, and after that a group set off for Krusevac village in order to fire at Serb homes in Krusevac, Dubocak, so that they had no choice but to leave their homes. There is the example of Milovan Milosevic, there was a person who escaped from their car when they opened fired on them. He ran to his house and they killed him right outside the house. As for Stankovic, they were 3 or 4 kilometres away from the main road and the centre of Krusevac village. They didn't know what the facts were on the ground and what was going on along that ground and near any of the other homes. For that reason they stayed the entire day. During the night Stankovic and his son Ljubisa joined me on the way out of Gorazde [as interpreted]. We took a path through the woods in order to reach their home, and we managed to evacuate Leka and his family, his wife and two sons who were still in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what happened to the house afterwards, what did the KLA do to it?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: They destroyed all those houses. I saw a satellite image because this technology is available for actually getting a good look, and I realized when I looked at this image that none of the houses remained in the area covered by those 20 villages or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Nine pages forward to page 617 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just to be clear about the detail of that. There's a reference at line 24 to during the night Stankovic and his son Ljubisa joined me on the way out of Gorazde. Then the next line: "We managed to evacuate Leka and his family." Is Stankovic not Leka? Are they not the same person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's his eldest son, not from Gorazde village but from Gorazdovce village near Pec. I think it was a case of misinterpretation. I was with his eldest son from Pec. After this incident, after what happened to us in Krusevac we from the police came to Pec and locals from the area started reporting everything that had been happening to them that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a second. I'm just trying to be clear about the -- when you went through the woods, was there one person with you or two people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stankovic Ljubisa, Ljubo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So one person, and it was the father that you actually evacuated with his family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We reached their house. Stankovic Aleksa, Leka. In the house we find him, his wife, and their two sons; the third is with me, the one who had arrived with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I -- the position is now clear. Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We were to be moving to -- just one moment. Nine pages forward to page 617, item number 224 on the bottom, and this one as well -- which we do -- no, that's the B/C/S. We don't have the English of that. If we could have you -- first of all, is this -- let's -- no, we'll just have you read it. It's only, well, seven lines or so. If you could read the entry number 224 and tell us if you have any personal knowledge or awareness of this incident that is depicted here.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: "Between the 29th March and the 24th of September, 1998, on several occasions members of the KLA carried out terrorist attacks on the house of Desanka Paunovic from Rausic -- Novi Rausic village, Pec municipality. For this reason she had no choice but to leave with her family. After that members of the KLA took away all the movable property that was in the house and set fire to the house itself."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And -- go ahead. Finish the last two sections.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: "Investigating judge authorised officials of the secretariat of the interior in Pec to carry out an investigation. Criminal complaint KU 572/98 was filed against unknown perpetrators and was delivered to the district public prosecutor's office."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you know any of the persons involved and do you have a personal knowledge about the events that are depicted here?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. She is the daughter, sister-in-law, Paunovic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who I said had been kidnapped after we left. Desanka Paunovic left Pec together with my family and went to Serbia later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could move approximately 13 pages forward to page 630, item number 286. It's at the bottom of the page, sir. Could you read this entry for Glodjane, Pec, the 1st of November, 1998, and could you tell us if you have any personal knowledge or any additional facts to provide relating to this event depicted here.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: "On the 1st of November, 1998, at about 1330 hours, members of the KLA carried out a terrorist attack against members of the Ministry of the Interior in Glodjane village near Pec. During the attack Drasko Stosic, a policeman from the secretariat of interior of Pec sustained slight physical injuries. No on-site investigation was carried out for security concerns. As I pointed out before, what happened. A person from Kosuric reported mistreatment, having been mistreated, and then we were off to Glodjane village. Once the complaint had been lodged. As soon as we had arrived outside the church in Glodjane, a vehicle showed up from the direction of Nepolje and discoursed four persons who immediately opened fire on our vehicle and the men in it. We were unable to fire back because there were two women and a man right there in the field or on a meadow. They then went Jablanica. They drove past the houses there and they used a hand-held launcher to fire a missile. They hit something that was just off the road, but a piece of shrapnel hit Drasko Stosic."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If we could move ahead eight pages to page 638, item number 321 on the overview entitled: "Rausic, Pec, 25th November 1998." Could you read for us this entry and tell us if this is one of the events that you have offered your testimony on here today relating to KLA activities against ethnic Albanians.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: That's right. "On the 25th of November, 1998, according to the report submitted by the injured party Gashi Ganija, a civilian, members of the KLA carried out an attack with four shells and they shot from automatic weapons at the village of Rausic because the villagers of the said village handed over weapons to the police. Members of the OSCE mission were informed about the incident."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you have any other further knowledge or details to provide about this event?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: I was present, as I've already pointed out, during the on-site investigation because at that time I was in the Celopek police department. I know Gashi Ganija because we did some shopping at his shop. We bought things that we needed at home, and also when we were in the area we would stop by, we would stop at his store. It is for that reason that they were warning him that he should not let us into his store.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we go on, page 681, item 504. I believe this might also be an event that you have offered your testimony on. Could you, since we don't have a translation of this either, could you briefly read for us this incident and tell us if indeed it is one that you have made reference to and what other personal details you can provide based on your recollections of the same.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: 504 you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: "On the 5th of March, on the 5th of March, 1999, around 2015 hours in the street of the Army of Yugoslavia number 73, members of the KLA carried out a terrorist attack against the Slavica catering facility by throwing a hand-grenade through the shop window. Due to the explosion of the hand-grenade in the store, grievous bodily injuries were sustained by Dejan Mijatovic, Bogicevic Dejan, and Kovacevic Milivoje, all of them from Pec; and light bodily injuries were sustained by Mitrovic Ivica, Markovic Slavica, and Bogicevic Zelimir. Markovic Slavica is the owner of this store. The on-site investigation was carried out by the investigating judge of the district court from Pec in the presence of members of the verification mission of the OSCE. A criminal complaint was filed."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is this the incident of the Slavica a soldier that you had previously identified?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: That's right. I've already mentioned that. I stopped at that shop and I know the persons there, I know the owner and other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could move ahead three pages to page 684, item number 515. Could you read for the record this item for Zlopek, Pec, the 9th of March, 1999, and tell us if you can provide any additional details based on your personal knowledge and information relating to the event that is set forth here.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: "On the 9th of March, 1999, around 6.30, Kocan Hashim [phoen] set out from the village of Zlopek on a bicycle in the direction of Pec where he had worked. A kilometre away from his house in the village of Zlopek, the injured party was abducted by armed members of the KLA and they took him in an unknown direction. His fate is unknown. An on-site investigation was not carried out for security reasons. A criminal complaint was filed KU 136/99 against perpetrators unknown and submitted to the district public prosecutor's office in Pec."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge or details to supplement what is set forth herein relating to this event?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: His wife happened to see me in Pec. I knew Hashim personally. He lived in Zlopek. That is near me, about a kilometre away. And when she and I were talking she asked me and said, Let us try to do whatever can be done in order to find him. Since she hadn't heard from him and she told me all about it, what happened. That's what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Was this individual ever located?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, he was never found.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One more item I'd like to look at on this overview, page 710, item number 631.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: "On the 8th of April, 1999, in the village of Ozrim members of the KLA carried out a terrorist attack against the patrol of the Ozrim police department. A policeman Esad Hasic sustained light injuries during this attack. On authority given by an investigating judge an on-site investigation was carried out by policemen of the secretariat of the interior of Pec. A criminal complaint KU 210/99 was filed against perpetrators unknown and submitted to the district public prosecutor's office Pec." I mentioned Esad Hasic, he was my deputy commander of my police squad in Celopek. I worked with him in 1998 I think. It was the beginning of 1998 or the end of 1997. That's when he started working at the Ozrim police department. After leaving Kosovo we met up at the place where he lives now. He said to me that his father and his step-mother had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Who killed his father and his step-mother, according to what he said?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: After we left Kosovo they were killed by the Siptars -- well, not Siptars, this group that was killing around Pec, a Siptar group that was called the Black Hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what ethnicity was Esad Hasic and his father and step-mother?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Muslim, but the only reason was because he had worked in the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir -- actually, while we have this on the screen I just realized, if we look at item number 632, Radovac, Pec, the 8th of April, 1999, is this the incident wherein Vidomir Salipur was killed?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, just to finish up a few points that I have left. We previously talked about a Minic Nebojsa and you said he had been in the police for two months before being let out. Was he an active or a reserve member of the SUP Pec during that two-month period when he was on duty with the SUP Pec?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Nebojsa Minic was from the reserve police. Since we had sustained big losses in our unit and we had a large number of wounded people, then the reserve police force was drawn upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in your testimony you had mentioned the M-70 rifle that all policemen in the SUP Pec were issued with. I don't know if you said it, but in the transcript it does not refer to the calibre. Could you tell us what the calibre that automatic rifle issued to the policemen of the SUP Pec would have been?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: I omitted to mention the calibre. The calibre was 7.62-millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And during the break I also looked back at the transcript and saw that I forgot to ask you how long did your training for the OPG take place?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: 15-day training.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And lastly, as part of the training you mentioned the stopping of vehicles. Would those have been situations where vehicles were fleeing from regular police forces?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: That's right. Rapid deployment check-points were placed, so when persons would move away from crime scenes or other sites we could put a check-point there because we did have mobile check-points on various roads within the Pec SUP, in order to avoid any undesirable consequences for the police organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the persons moving away from crime scenes in that scenario would be the perpetrators; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: That's right. Precisely because of such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nikcevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. There seems to be no Defence cross-examination. Mr. Nikcevic, you'll now be cross-examined by the Prosecutor, Mr. Hannis. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Nikcevic.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If I understand correctly, you joined the PJP in 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And then in 1999 you also became a member of an OPG?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what month in 1999 that was?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: The end of 1998 and the beginning of 1999, the very beginning. In December I completed my training and I became a member of the OPG.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what were you doing between 1992 and when you joined the OPG or became a member of the OPG? Were you working as a regular policeman in Celopek?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: That's right. I did regular police work. I worked in the sector, I did patrols, check-points, duty service, and other work.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And in 1998 between July and the end of October 1998, did you take part in any actions as a member of the PJP in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was that -- were any of those actions joint actions with the army, with the VJ?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: There were actions that we carried out with the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We'll probably get to some of those tomorrow because we're almost out of time for today, but tell me about the OPG. What exactly is that? If I understood what you said, this is a group of men who were drawn from the PJP. Is this a smaller group taken from the PJP?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: The OPG is -- OPG were not taken out of PJP ranks. They are still within the PJP, but they had undergone intensified training.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So is everybody who's in an OPG also a member of some PJP unit except they've had additional training over and above what the regular PJP members have?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: That's right. They stay in the same unit that they had been sent from. I was sent by my company commander and I returned to the same company.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And is the OPG some specialised group within the PJP that's called upon for special tasks or special assignments because they have had additional training?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Nothing is specialised. They just shouldered a burden that was greater than that shouldered by others. They bore the brunt of the work.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So did every -- did every PJP then have within it at least one OPG, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: All PJP from the 124th did. I think the others did too.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if you could help us out, what was the 124th?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's not a brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: At first we called it the intervention brigade, and then it was expanded into a detachment, whatever -- how should I know?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know when that change occurred?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And can you give me an example of the kind of task or job that an OPG might be given to do that couldn't be or wouldn't be done by just regular PJP personnel?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: OPG did not receive special tasks that were to be carried out. The OPG primarily was supposed to be in the forefront when we went into action and the other men were supposed to look at them but we did not really receive any independent special tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You wore the same kinds of uniforms as a regular PJP, correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You had the same kind of weapons and equipment?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: The same weapons, the same equipment, the same everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I guess I'm having a hard time understanding why this separate group of OPG is created. It sounds like there's really no difference between them. You didn't get any extra pay. What is the difference, just that extra training?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: From my point of view, that was the only thing. Now, how it was envisioned at a higher level, they're probably the only ones who know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Within your OPG did you have a commander who was different than your commander in the PJP?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC
utterances.text: No. My immediate superior was the company commander, Krsto Djuricic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, would this be an appropriate place to break for the day?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It would if I could understand the last point. Are you saying that he also led the OPG or was there some other platoon commander that led the OPG?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Our immediate superior was Krsto Djuricic as company commander. The OPG is -- the OPG was not platoon strength but squad strength.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hannis, there is pending a motion for addition of documents to the Lukic Defence Rule 65 ter list for the witness Marinkovic. Now, it was only filed yesterday, but are you in a position to say whether you have any comment or response to make?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure. Ms. Carter will be handling that witness, it was forwarded to her, but I haven't had a chance to discuss with her if she has a position to raise with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could you ask her, if possible, to respond at least informally to the Chamber today to let us know whether more time's necessary to consider it, whether there is no response, or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just so that we know where we are strategically because this is a witness scheduled for this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I will. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Nikcevic, we have to interrupt our proceedings now for the day. That completes our work for the day, which means that you will require to return tomorrow to complete your evidence. Meanwhile, it is vital that you have no communication with anyone at all, anyone at all, about any aspect of the evidence in this whole case. You may communicate with whoever you like about whatever other subjects you wish except the evidence in the case. We will resume at 9.00 tomorrow, 9.00 in the morning tomorrow, in this courtroom. Now would you please leave the courtroom with the usher and we will see you again at 9.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 27th day of February, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 24

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
